principles.body: discovering how you want to shape your life is hard! some people get lucky and find it early, but for most people, it can take years of diligent and relentless searching. in order to find out what to work on, just keep working. pick something and go forward. cast a wide net early and take swings.
principles.source: Paul Graham - How to Do Great Work

principles.principle: be overly delusional with your life.
principles.body: be so delusional with your life that you have no other choice but to succeed. there will also be people who don't see the future you do, but that should never diminish your light.

principles.principle: you can become paralyzed if you overanalyze.
principles.body: thinking can be productive, but it can also be paralyzing. it makes you feel productive, but it can also cause you to feel stuck. don't overanalyze to the point that you are paralyzed.

principles.principle: life is meant to be messy.
principles.body: we are in a decade where everything seems to have the ability to be optimized. but life is meant to be unpredictable, messy. i'm learning to embrace it!

i harp on this often, but my history minor provided me with so much more than i could've imagined. empathy is one of them. learning to understand people from the past without having all the tools to live through it helps you understand empathy in today's world.

principles.principle: some areas require order, others require chaos.
principles.body: not everything needs a procedure. not everything can be left alone. it's an important distinction to choose which areas need what.

principles.source: A quote from my Stanford admissions officer sent me when I was accepted.

principles.principle: allow people to change & allow your perception to change about them too.
principles.body: one of my own principles that i've been quoting SOOO often! anticipate a new Substack about this soon!
